3337f1e5-3b55-5e56-8003-d80e2a1293c2.title: Swapping the Order of Integration by Changing the Projection Type

e-12401.knowledge_point: Swapping the Order of Integration by Changing the Projection Type
e-12401.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/5a19eefe8fdcd63ef9f8a35bf4517b022ab2c35b5fccd06e1e797f67e567653a.png)

The triple integral of $f(x,y,z)$ over the region $R$ (shown above) can be expressed as the following repeated integral:

$$
\iiint\limits_R  f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}V
=
\int_0^1\int_{\sqrt{z}}^1\int_0^{y^2-z} f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}z
$$

Rewrite this repeated integral by integrating first with respect to $x,$ then $z,$ and then $y.$
e-12401.worked_solution:
From the given repeated integral, we see that $R$ can be written as a type II region as follows:

$$
R = \big\{ (x,y,z) \: : \: 0 \leq z \leq 1, \:\: \sqrt{z} \leq y \leq 1, \:\: 0 \leq x \leq y^2-z \big\}
$$

We wish to rewrite our triple integral as follows:

$$
\iiint\limits_R f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}V
=
\int_a^b\int_{v_1(y)}^{v_2(y)}\int_{u_1(y,z)}^{u_2(y,z)} f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}y
$$

Since both repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $x,$ the $x$-limits remain the same as before:

$$
\iiint\limits_R f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}V
=
\int_a^b\int_{v_1(y)}^{v_2(y)}\int_0^{y^2-z} f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}y
$$

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $yz$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/ec195fe4aa1bec5221ec25a1921dfe36e78db34ad3e295fec541c1d05a85d60d.png)

The region $D$ is a type II region in the $yz$-plane:

$$
D = \big\{ (y,z) \: : \: 0 \leq z \leq 1, \:\: \sqrt{z} \leq y \leq 1 \big\}
$$

To change the order of integration from $\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}z$ to $\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}y,$ we write $D$ as a type I region.

Notice that the top boundary of the region, written in the form $z=z(y),$ is 

$$
y=\sqrt{z}
\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad
z = y^2
$$

and the bottom boundary of the region is

$$
z=0.
$$

Then, the type I representation of the region $D$ is

$$
D = \big\{ (y,z) \: : \: 0 \leq y \leq 1, \:\: 0 \leq z\leq y^2 \big\},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/841f014cae7bb224b6f743a86583cb0a70a423d60176b2efd6482d155aa020bc.png)

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\iiint\limits_R f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}V
=

\int_0^1 \int_{0}^{y^2} \int_0^{y^2-z} f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}y.
$$

before.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/5907cf8a9103cc9a639fd8078da3646cc0395d28827f58c0f1beef0a1c06645b.png)

The triple integral of $f(x,y,z)$ over the region $R$ (shown above) can be expressed as the following repeated integral:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{y}{\int }_{0}^{{y}^{2}-{x}^{2}}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y
$$

Rewrite this repeated integral by integrating first with respect to $z,$ then $y,$ and then $x.$

Question 1

The triple integral of f(x,y,z) over the region R (shown above) can be expressed as the following repeated integral:

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∫01∫0y∫0y2−x2f(x,y,z)dzdxdy

Rewrite this repeated integral by integrating first with respect to z, then y, and then x.

a
 ∫01∫x2x∫0y2−x2f(x,y,z)dzdydx
b
 ∫01∫x1∫0y2−x2f(x,y,z)dzdydx
c
 ∫01∫0x∫0y2−x2f(x,y,z)dzdydx
d
 ∫01∫0x∫0y2−x2f(x,y,z)dzdydx
e
 ∫01∫x1∫0y2−x2f(x,y,z)dzdydx
Submit

decision.explanation: The original bounds describe 0 ≤ x ≤ y ≤ 1 and 0 ≤ z ≤ y² − x². Reversing the order over the xy-projection gives 0 ≤ x ≤ 1 and x ≤ y ≤ 1, while the z-bounds remain unchanged. Thus option b has the required order.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/5907cf8a9103cc9a639fd8078da3646cc0395d28827f58c0f1beef0a1c06645b.png)

The triple integral of $f(x,y,z)$ over the region $R$ (shown above) can be expressed as the following repeated integral:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{y}{\int }_{0}^{{y}^{2}-{x}^{2}}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y
$$

Rewrite this repeated integral by integrating first with respect to $z,$ then $y,$ and then $x.$
after.worked_solution:
From the given repeated integral, we see that $R$ can be written as a type I region as follows:

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,\,0\le x\le y,\,\,0\le z\le {y}^{2}-{x}^{2}}
$$

We wish to rewrite our triple integral as follows:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(x)}^{{v}_{2}(x)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(x,y)}^{{u}_{2}(x,y)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x
$$

Since both repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $z,$ the $z$-limits remain the same as before:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(x)}^{{v}_{2}(x)}{\int }_{0}^{{y}^{2}-{x}^{2}}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x
$$

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $xy$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/a89646433c8851f66c94092b75fae7b46b01f31c69ca03d338464b87bd7f5df4.png)

The region $D$ is a type II region in the $xy$-plane:

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,\,0\le x\le y}
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y$ to $\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x,$ we write $D$ as a type I region.

Notice that the bottom boundary of the region, written in the form $y=y(x),$ is 

$$
x=y\,⟹\,y=x
$$

and the top boundary of the region is

$$
y=1.
$$

Then, the type I representation of the region $D$ is

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,\,x\le y\le 1},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/1604e44050208cfb3b4dd81d35bff9769c7498d8304583d5ba92ad4b2f62fd05.png)

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{x}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{{y}^{2}-{x}^{2}}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.
$$

Question 1
?

The triple integral of f(x,y,z) over the region R (shown above) can be expressed as the following repeated integral:

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∫01∫0y∫0y2−x2f(x,y,z)dzdxdy

Rewrite this repeated integral by integrating first with respect to z, then y, and then x.

a
 ∫01∫x2x∫0y2−x2f(x,y,z)dzdydx
b
 ∫01∫x1∫0y2−x2f(x,y,z)dzdydx
c
 ∫01∫0x∫0y2−x2f(x,y,z)dzdydx
d
 ∫01∫0x∫0y2−x2f(x,y,z)dzdydx
e
 ∫01∫x1∫0y2−x2f(x,y,z)dzdydx
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

From the given repeated integral, we see that R can be written as a type I region as follows:

R={(x,y,z):0≤y≤1,0≤x≤y,0≤z≤y2−x2}

We wish to rewrite our triple integral as follows:

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∫ab∫v1(x)v2(x)∫u1(x,y)u2(x,y)f(x,y,z)dzdydx

Since both repeated integrals first integrate with respect to z, the z-limits remain the same as before:

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∫ab∫v1(x)v2(x)∫0y2−x2f(x,y,z)dzdydx

Now, we consider the projection D of R onto the xy-plane shown below.

The region D is a type II region in the xy-plane:

D={(x,y):0≤y≤1,0≤x≤y}

To change the order of integration from dzdxdy to dzdydx, we write D as a type I region.

Notice that the bottom boundary of the region, written in the form y=y(x), is

x=y⟹y=x

and the top boundary of the region is

y=1.

Then, the type I representation of the region D is

D={(x,y):0≤x≤1,x≤y≤1},

as shown below.

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain ∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∫01∫x1∫0y2−x2f(x,y,z)dzdydx.

content.knowledge_point: Swapping the Order of Integration by Changing the Projection Type
content.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/5907cf8a9103cc9a639fd8078da3646cc0395d28827f58c0f1beef0a1c06645b.png)

The triple integral of $f(x,y,z)$ over the region $R$ (shown above) can be expressed as the following repeated integral:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{y}{\int }_{0}^{{y}^{2}-{x}^{2}}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y
$$

Rewrite this repeated integral by integrating first with respect to $z,$ then $y,$ and then $x.$
content.worked_solution:
From the given repeated integral, we see that $R$ can be written as a type I region as follows:

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,\,0\le x\le y,\,\,0\le z\le {y}^{2}-{x}^{2}}
$$

We wish to rewrite our triple integral as follows:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(x)}^{{v}_{2}(x)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(x,y)}^{{u}_{2}(x,y)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x
$$

Since both repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $z,$ the $z$-limits remain the same as before:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(x)}^{{v}_{2}(x)}{\int }_{0}^{{y}^{2}-{x}^{2}}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x
$$

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $xy$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/a89646433c8851f66c94092b75fae7b46b01f31c69ca03d338464b87bd7f5df4.png)

The region $D$ is a type II region in the $xy$-plane:

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,\,0\le x\le y}
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y$ to $\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x,$ we write $D$ as a type I region.

Notice that the bottom boundary of the region, written in the form $y=y(x),$ is 

$$
x=y\,⟹\,y=x
$$

and the top boundary of the region is

$$
y=1.
$$

Then, the type I representation of the region $D$ is

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,\,x\le y\le 1},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/1604e44050208cfb3b4dd81d35bff9769c7498d8304583d5ba92ad4b2f62fd05.png)

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{x}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{{y}^{2}-{x}^{2}}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.
$$

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∫01∫0x2∫0x2+yf(x,y,z)dzdydx

Rewrite this repeated integral by integrating first with respect to z, then x, and then y.

a
∫01∫0y∫0x2+yf(x,y,z)dzdxdy
b
∫01∫y1∫0x2+yf(x,y,z)dzdxdy
c
∫01∫0y∫0x2+yf(x,y,z)dzdxdy
d

e

decision.explanation: The xy-projection satisfies 0 ≤ x ≤ 1 and 0 ≤ y ≤ x². Since x is nonnegative, reversing these bounds gives 0 ≤ y ≤ 1 and √y ≤ x ≤ 1. The z-bounds remain 0 ≤ z ≤ x² + y, so option d is correct.

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/c420d45ca9418fd29889d91a49cce4ae80bb71bdfd4e4aa701b495cc8d87335f.png)

The triple integral of $f(x,y,z)$ over the region $R$ (shown above) can be expressed as the following repeated integral:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{{x}^{2}}{\int }_{0}^{{x}^{2}+y}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x
$$

Rewrite this repeated integral by integrating first with respect to $z,$ then $x,$ and then $y.$
after.worked_solution:
From the given repeated integral, we see that $R$ can be written as a type I region as follows:

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,\,0\le y\le {x}^{2},\,\,0\le z\le {x}^{2}+y}
$$

We wish to rewrite our triple integral as follows:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(y)}^{{v}_{2}(y)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(x,y)}^{{u}_{2}(x,y)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y
$$

Since both repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $z,$ the $z$-limits remain the same as before:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(y)}^{{v}_{2}(y)}{\int }_{0}^{{x}^{2}+y}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y
$$

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $xy$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/8b7cfa72ed3dbfb121039c6e64b843d83489878a9f457fb1386e455e7d9649ec.png)

The region $D$ is a type I region in the $xy$-plane:

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,\,0\le y\le {x}^{2}}
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x$ to $\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y,$ we write $D$ as a type II region.

Notice that the left boundary of the region, written in the form $x=x(y),$ is 

$$
y={x}^{2}\,⟹\,x=\sqrt{y}
$$

and the right boundary of the region is

$$
x=1.
$$

Then, the type II representation of the region $D$ is

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,\,\sqrt{y}\le x\le 1},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/f49af5da2e4f1f281700e16c4659fabfcd0b15661947ca985d38f208f8563877.png)

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{\sqrt{y}}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{{x}^{2}+y}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.
$$

EXPLANATION

From the given repeated integral, we see that R can be written as a type I region as follows:

R={(x,y,z):0≤x≤1,0≤y≤x2,0≤z≤x2+y}

We wish to rewrite our triple integral as follows:

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∫ab∫v1(y)v2(y)∫u1(x,y)u2(x,y)f(x,y,z)dzdxdy

Since both repeated integrals first integrate with respect to z, the z-limits remain the same as before:

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∫ab∫v1(y)v2(y)∫0x2+yf(x,y,z)dzdxdy

Now, we consider the projection D of R onto the xy-plane shown below.

The region D is a type I region in the xy-plane:

D={(x,y):0≤x≤1,0≤y≤x2}

To change the order of integration from dzdydx to dzdxdy, we write D as a type II region.

Notice that the left boundary of the region, written in the form x=x(y), is

y=x2⟹x=y

and the right boundary of the region is

x=1.

Then, the type II representation of the region D is

D={(x,y):0≤y≤1,y≤x≤1},

as shown below.

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain ∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∫01∫y1∫0x2+yf(x,y,z)dzdxdy.

content.knowledge_point: Swapping the Order of Integration by Changing the Projection Type
content.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/c420d45ca9418fd29889d91a49cce4ae80bb71bdfd4e4aa701b495cc8d87335f.png)

The triple integral of $f(x,y,z)$ over the region $R$ (shown above) can be expressed as the following repeated integral:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{{x}^{2}}{\int }_{0}^{{x}^{2}+y}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x
$$

Rewrite this repeated integral by integrating first with respect to $z,$ then $x,$ and then $y.$
content.worked_solution:
From the given repeated integral, we see that $R$ can be written as a type I region as follows:

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,\,0\le y\le {x}^{2},\,\,0\le z\le {x}^{2}+y}
$$

We wish to rewrite our triple integral as follows:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(y)}^{{v}_{2}(y)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(x,y)}^{{u}_{2}(x,y)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y
$$

Since both repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $z,$ the $z$-limits remain the same as before:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(y)}^{{v}_{2}(y)}{\int }_{0}^{{x}^{2}+y}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y
$$

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $xy$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/8b7cfa72ed3dbfb121039c6e64b843d83489878a9f457fb1386e455e7d9649ec.png)

The region $D$ is a type I region in the $xy$-plane:

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,\,0\le y\le {x}^{2}}
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x$ to $\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y,$ we write $D$ as a type II region.

Notice that the left boundary of the region, written in the form $x=x(y),$ is 

$$
y={x}^{2}\,⟹\,x=\sqrt{y}
$$

and the right boundary of the region is

$$
x=1.
$$

Then, the type II representation of the region $D$ is

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,\,\sqrt{y}\le x\le 1},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/f49af5da2e4f1f281700e16c4659fabfcd0b15661947ca985d38f208f8563877.png)

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{\sqrt{y}}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{{x}^{2}+y}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.
$$

Rewrite this repeated integral by integrating first with respect to x, then z, and then y.

decision.explanation: The yz-projection satisfies 0 ≤ z ≤ 1 and 0 ≤ y ≤ ∛z. Equivalently, 0 ≤ y ≤ 1 and y³ ≤ z ≤ 1. The x-bounds remain 1 + y − z ≤ x ≤ 2, giving option a.

after.name: Question 3
after.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/024df0fe0a965feba2177adfac8bbd658fc90f4775a4707f13eba1ef2cb94702.png)

The triple integral of $f(x,y,z)$ over the region $R$ (shown above) can be expressed as the following repeated integral:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt[3]{z}}{\int }_{1+y-z}^{2}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z
$$

Rewrite this repeated integral by integrating first with respect to $x,$ then $z,$ and then $y.$
after.worked_solution:
From the given repeated integral, we see that $R$ can be written as a type II region as follows:

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le z\le 1,\,\,0\le y\le \sqrt[3]{z},\,\,1+y-z\le x\le 2}
$$

We wish to rewrite our triple integral as follows:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(y)}^{{v}_{2}(y)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(y,z)}^{{u}_{2}(y,z)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y
$$

Since both repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $x,$ the $x$-limits remain the same as before:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(y)}^{{v}_{2}(y)}{\int }_{1+y-z}^{2}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y
$$

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $yz$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/8fff232443e6da697862c2e85a9d3abfe0554b80c2fcbfa8c93de42b94a45691.png)

The region $D$ is a type II region in the $yz$-plane:

$$
D={(y,z)\,:\,0\le z\le 1,\,\,0\le y\le \sqrt[3]{z}}
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z$ to $\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y,$ we write $D$ as a type I region.

Notice that the bottom boundary of the region, written in the form $z=z(y),$ is 

$$
y=\sqrt[3]{z}\,⟹\,z={y}^{3}
$$

and the top boundary of the region is

$$
z=1.
$$

Then, the type I representation of the region $D$ is

$$
D={(y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,\,{y}^{3}\le z\le 1},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/726ff420cae25c40f212714141a134fab84633cca7f49bdd268f0668d5248766.png)

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{{y}^{3}}^{1}{\int }_{1+y-z}^{2}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y.
$$

Question 3

The triple integral of f(x,y,z) over the region R (shown above) can be expressed as the following repeated integral:

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∫01∫0z3∫1+y−z2f(x,y,z)dxdydz

Rewrite this repeated integral by integrating first with respect to x, then z, and then y.

a
 ∫01∫y31∫1+y−z2f(x,y,z)dxdzdy
b
 ∫01∫0y3∫1+y−z32f(x,y,z)dxdzdy
c
 ∫01∫11+y∫1+y−z2f(x,y,z)dxdzdy
d
 ∫01∫0y3∫1+y−z2f(x,y,z)dxdzdy
e
 ∫01∫y31∫1+y−z32f(x,y,z)dxdzdy
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

From the given repeated integral, we see that R can be written as a type II region as follows:

R={(x,y,z):0≤z≤1,0≤y≤z3,1+y−z≤x≤2}

We wish to rewrite our triple integral as follows:

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∫ab∫v1(y)v2(y)∫u1(y,z)u2(y,z)f(x,y,z)dxdzdy

Since both repeated integrals first integrate with respect to x, the x-limits remain the same as before:

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∫ab∫v1(y)v2(y)∫1+y−z2f(x,y,z)dxdzdy

Now, we consider the projection D of R onto the yz-plane shown below.

The region D is a type II region in the yz-plane:

D={(y,z):0≤z≤1,0≤y≤z3}

To change the order of integration from dxdydz to dxdzdy, we write D as a type I region.

Notice that the bottom boundary of the region, written in the form z=z(y), is

y=z3⟹z=y3

and the top boundary of the region is

z=1.

Then, the type I representation of the region D is

D={(y,z):0≤y≤1,y3≤z≤1},

as shown below.

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain ∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∫01∫y31∫1+y−z2f(x,y,z)dxdzdy.

content.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/024df0fe0a965feba2177adfac8bbd658fc90f4775a4707f13eba1ef2cb94702.png)

The triple integral of $f(x,y,z)$ over the region $R$ (shown above) can be expressed as the following repeated integral:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt[3]{z}}{\int }_{1+y-z}^{2}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z
$$

Rewrite this repeated integral by integrating first with respect to $x,$ then $z,$ and then $y.$
content.worked_solution:
From the given repeated integral, we see that $R$ can be written as a type II region as follows:

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le z\le 1,\,\,0\le y\le \sqrt[3]{z},\,\,1+y-z\le x\le 2}
$$

We wish to rewrite our triple integral as follows:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(y)}^{{v}_{2}(y)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(y,z)}^{{u}_{2}(y,z)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y
$$

Since both repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $x,$ the $x$-limits remain the same as before:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(y)}^{{v}_{2}(y)}{\int }_{1+y-z}^{2}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y
$$

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $yz$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/8fff232443e6da697862c2e85a9d3abfe0554b80c2fcbfa8c93de42b94a45691.png)

The region $D$ is a type II region in the $yz$-plane:

$$
D={(y,z)\,:\,0\le z\le 1,\,\,0\le y\le \sqrt[3]{z}}
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z$ to $\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y,$ we write $D$ as a type I region.

Notice that the bottom boundary of the region, written in the form $z=z(y),$ is 

$$
y=\sqrt[3]{z}\,⟹\,z={y}^{3}
$$

and the top boundary of the region is

$$
z=1.
$$

Then, the type I representation of the region $D$ is

$$
D={(y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,\,{y}^{3}\le z\le 1},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/726ff420cae25c40f212714141a134fab84633cca7f49bdd268f0668d5248766.png)

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{{y}^{3}}^{1}{\int }_{1+y-z}^{2}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y.
$$

The triple integral of f(x,y,z) over the region R (shown above) can be expressed as the following repeated integral:

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∫01∫01−y2∫01−x2−y2+1f(x,y,z)dzdxdy

Rewrite this repeated integral by integrating first with respect to z, then y, and then x.

a
 ∫01∫01−x2∫01−x2−y2+1f(x,y,z)dzdydx
b
 ∫01∫01−x2∫0x2+y2f(x,y,z)dzdydx
c
 ∫01∫01−x2∫01−x2−y2f(x,y,z)dzdydx
d
 ∫01∫1x2∫01−x2−y2+1f(x,y,z)dzdydx
e
 ∫01∫1−x21∫0x2+y2f(x,y,z)dzdydx
Submit

decision.explanation: The xy-projection is the quarter disk x ≥ 0, y ≥ 0, x² + y² ≤ 1. Reversing its bounds gives 0 ≤ x ≤ 1 and 0 ≤ y ≤ √(1 − x²). The z-bounds remain 0 ≤ z ≤ √(1 − x² − y²) + 1, so option a is correct.

after.name: Question 4
after.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/c72489a2d33a181fe7bc07d5cc017b93daccac51889cbb61edd64d4ee34429df.png)

The triple integral of $f(x,y,z)$ over the region $R$ (shown above) can be expressed as the following repeated integral:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{1-{y}^{2}}}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}}+1}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y
$$

Rewrite this repeated integral by integrating first with respect to $z,$ then $y,$ and then $x.$
after.worked_solution:
From the given repeated integral, we see that $R$ can be written as a type I region as follows:

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,\,0\le y\le \sqrt{1-{y}^{2}},\,\,0\le z\le \sqrt{1-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}}+1}
$$

We wish to rewrite our triple integral as follows:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(x)}^{{v}_{2}(x)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(x,y)}^{{u}_{2}(x,y)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x
$$

Since both repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $z,$ the $z$-limits remain the same as before:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(x)}^{{v}_{2}(x)}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}}+1}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x
$$

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $xy$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/98aa4c0a436e4649ccd3d48a53fbf94b0341bf30b95745c4d052381680d223cf.png)

The region $D$ is a type II region in the $xy$-plane:

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,\,0\le x\le \sqrt{1-{y}^{2}}}
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y$ to $\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x,$ we write $D$ as a type I region.

Notice that the top boundary of the region, written in the form $y=y(x),$ is 

$$
x=\sqrt{1-{y}^{2}}\,⟹\,y=\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}
$$

and the bottom boundary of the region is

$$
y=0.
$$

Then, the type I representation of the region $D$ is

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,\,0\le y\le \sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/47380c108c5b271761de2a027399bbd5981f2a9bdff21e498d73d0b430d070c7.png)

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}}+1}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.
$$

Question 4

The triple integral of f(x,y,z) over the region R (shown above) can be expressed as the following repeated integral:

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∫01∫01−y2∫01−x2−y2+1f(x,y,z)dzdxdy

Rewrite this repeated integral by integrating first with respect to z, then y, and then x.

a
 ∫01∫01−x2∫01−x2−y2+1f(x,y,z)dzdydx
b
 ∫01∫01−x2∫0x2+y2f(x,y,z)dzdydx
c
 ∫01∫01−x2∫01−x2−y2f(x,y,z)dzdydx
d
 ∫01∫1x2∫01−x2−y2+1f(x,y,z)dzdydx
e
 ∫01∫1−x21∫0x2+y2f(x,y,z)dzdydx
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

From the given repeated integral, we see that R can be written as a type I region as follows:

R={(x,y,z):0≤x≤1,0≤y≤1−y2,0≤z≤1−x2−y2+1}

We wish to rewrite our triple integral as follows:

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∫ab∫v1(x)v2(x)∫u1(x,y)u2(x,y)f(x,y,z)dzdydx

Since both repeated integrals first integrate with respect to z, the z-limits remain the same as before:

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∫ab∫v1(x)v2(x)∫01−x2−y2+1f(x,y,z)dzdydx

Now, we consider the projection D of R onto the xy-plane shown below.

The region D is a type II region in the xy-plane:

D={(x,y):0≤y≤1,0≤x≤1−y2}

To change the order of integration from dzdxdy to dzdydx, we write D as a type I region.

Notice that the top boundary of the region, written in the form y=y(x), is

x=1−y2⟹y=1−x2

and the bottom boundary of the region is

y=0.

Then, the type I representation of the region D is

D={(x,y):0≤x≤1,0≤y≤1−x2},

as shown below.

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain ∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∫01∫01−x2∫01−x2−y2+1f(x,y,z)dzdydx.

verification.explanation: Option a matches the original quarter-disk projection: 0 ≤ x ≤ 1 and 0 ≤ y ≤ √(1 − x²), with the z-bounds unchanged. The worked solution’s final integral confirms this; its initial region description contains a typo. The observed incorrect submission was option e, not a.

content.knowledge_point: Swapping the Order of Integration by Changing the Projection Type
content.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/c72489a2d33a181fe7bc07d5cc017b93daccac51889cbb61edd64d4ee34429df.png)

The triple integral of $f(x,y,z)$ over the region $R$ (shown above) can be expressed as the following repeated integral:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{1-{y}^{2}}}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}}+1}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y
$$

Rewrite this repeated integral by integrating first with respect to $z,$ then $y,$ and then $x.$
content.worked_solution:
From the given repeated integral, we see that $R$ can be written as a type I region as follows:

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,\,0\le y\le \sqrt{1-{y}^{2}},\,\,0\le z\le \sqrt{1-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}}+1}
$$

We wish to rewrite our triple integral as follows:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(x)}^{{v}_{2}(x)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(x,y)}^{{u}_{2}(x,y)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x
$$

Since both repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $z,$ the $z$-limits remain the same as before:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(x)}^{{v}_{2}(x)}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}}+1}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x
$$

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $xy$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/98aa4c0a436e4649ccd3d48a53fbf94b0341bf30b95745c4d052381680d223cf.png)

The region $D$ is a type II region in the $xy$-plane:

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,\,0\le x\le \sqrt{1-{y}^{2}}}
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y$ to $\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x,$ we write $D$ as a type I region.

Notice that the top boundary of the region, written in the form $y=y(x),$ is 

$$
x=\sqrt{1-{y}^{2}}\,⟹\,y=\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}
$$

and the bottom boundary of the region is

$$
y=0.
$$

Then, the type I representation of the region $D$ is

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,\,0\le y\le \sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/47380c108c5b271761de2a027399bbd5981f2a9bdff21e498d73d0b430d070c7.png)

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}}+1}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.
$$
